title: Hyundai explores investment in Posco graphite project in Vietnam
summary: Hyundai Motor Group is considering an investment in Posco Future M's planned synthetic graphite business in Vietnam. The proposed investment is 100 billion won, (around 67.6 million euros). In return, Hyundai is to receive preferred purchasing rights for the anode material.

title: VW launches the ID. ERA 5X in China with pricing
summary: The VW ID. ERA 5X costs around 13,530 euros in China at market launch and offers more interior space than a VW ID. Tiguan despite its smaller dimensions. This is made possible by the new Compact Main Platform, which debuts with the ID. ERA 5X. The China SUV can also be equipped with partially automated assistance systems.

title: VW’s Scout brand begins production of first test vehicles at new US plant
summary: Volkswagen's revived US brand Scout has begun assembling the first validation vehicles at its new plant in Blythewood, South Carolina. As the factory is still under construction, it will be several more months before Scout vehicles are running off production lines in series.

title: UK funds project for recovering nickel, cobalt and copper
summary: ReOre Technologies, an Altilium Group company focused on recovering critical minerals from mining waste, has announced it will lead a new UK government-backed project to unlock domestic supplies of nickel, cobalt and copper. For the two-year Cascade project, ReOre is collaborating with project partners Aberdeen Minerals and Camborne School of Mines, supported by the Battery Innovation Programme.

title: British Gas orders nearly 2,000 VW Transporters, some of which are electric
summary: Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles has delivered 1,986 new transporters to British Gas. The fleet includes both electric Transporters and diesel models. The companies have not disclosed the number of purely electric vehicles.

title: Mercedes board threatens to close German plants and stop investments in Germany
summary: Mercedes-Benz is temporarily halting its investments in Germany and putting plants up for sale. The move is a response by management to the protracted negotiations with the union over what Mercedes says are excessively high labor costs. The company's board insists on cuts to keep German production competitive.

title: Lucid Air Grand Touring: a long-distance champion with plenty of power
summary: For two weeks, we travelled with this luxury sedan from California. The Lucid Air impresses with its long-distance capability, an extremely quiet interior, and intuitive controls. However, it also has a few weaknesses that shouldn’t exist at this price point.

title: UK depot charging scheme reopens – with reduced funding rate
summary: The UK Government has reopened applications for the section round of its Depot Charging Scheme, which provides funding for businesses installing charging infrastructure for electric vans and HGVs. However, the grant rate has been reduced from 70 to 60 per cent of eligible costs.

title: VW ID. Tiguan enters series production
summary: Just a few weeks after the unveiling of the VW ID. Tiguan, Volkswagen has now started series production of the electric SUV at its Emden plant. Although the vehicle will not be available at dealerships until early 2027, thousands of pre-orders have already been placed.

title: India: Olectra deploys 35 electric buses in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar
summary: Indian electric commercial vehicle manufacturer Olectra Greentech Limited, a subsidiary of Megha Engineering and Infrastructures Limited (MEIL), has commissioned 35 electric buses in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, a city in the western state of Maharashtra. The new buses serve the city's public transport fleet.

title: Smatrics EnBW deploys first XCharge charger with 480 kW in Austria
summary: Smatrics EnBW has opened a new fast-charging location in Vienna with eight charging points. There, the operator is using XCharge's new C7 generation for the first time in Austria, offering charging power of up to 480 kW.

title: Fraunhofer IFAM researches e-motors with fewer critical raw materials
summary: Fraunhofer IFAM is building new research infrastructure in Dresden for electric motors that are designed to use fewer critical raw materials. The SIREN project focuses on, among other things, drives without rare earth elements and aluminium as a substitute for copper in the windings.

title: Mission accomplished: Rimac discontinues Nevera ahead of schedule
summary: Mate Rimac has announced the premature end of production for his company's hypercar, the Rimac Nevera, after just 71 units instead of the planned 190. However, Rimac's founder does not wish to classify this as a failure, but rather as "mission accomplished." His perspective on electromobility today seems different from when the Nevera project began in 2017.

title: QuantumScape launches open platform for sulphide-based solid-state batteries
summary: The Volkswagen partner has unveiled an open platform for sulphide-based solid-state batteries. It aims to create new licensing and co-development opportunities for existing customers - and allow the integration of third-party components.

title: VW scraps ‘Gamechanger’ manufacturing project amid cost-cutting drive
summary: Volkswagen is scrapping the planned manufacturing concept "Gamechanger" and abandoning the construction of a large-scale casting center at its Wolfsburg headquarters. With the project, the group aimed to make the production of future electric vehicles on the new SSP platform significantly more efficient and cost-effective. Now, cost-cutting measures are forcing the company to change course.

title: Up to €6,000 for EVs: Luxembourg extends incentive scheme
summary: Luxembourg extends state subsidies for electric cars, e-bikes, and wallboxes under the 'Klimabonus Mobilitéit' scheme until 2030. For new cars, up to €6,000 is available depending on consumption, and from 2027, this amount can even be deducted directly from the invoice at the dealer.

title: Attacks in Ukraine spark fresh wiring harness shortages
summary: Missing wire harnesses from Ukraine are once again disrupting European car production. BMW had to cancel shifts at several locations, while Skoda's affected models included the electric Enyaq and Elroq.

title: EU and UK could delay mutual EV tariffs once more
summary: The EU Commission is reportedly considering postponing tariffs on the electric car trade with the UK, which were planned for 2027. London is also said to support a delay. The automotive industry warns of competitive disadvantages due to the looming ten per cent duty.

title: VW Anhui: no plans to launch new electric models until 2028
summary: According to insiders, Chinese majority-owned VW subsidiary Volkswagen Anhui will not launch any new ID. UNYX models in 2027 and 2028. The current lineup of four EVs will thus remain unchanged for the time being. The joint venture with JAC is significantly missing its sales targets.

title: Daimler Buses CEO Till Oberwörder: full focus on battery-electric buses
summary: Daimler Buses will no longer invest in new diesel city buses. Instead, the Mercedes-Benz eCitaro will become the sole main player in urban public transport. We met with CEO Till Oberwörder for an interview and discussed the new platform strategy, the future qualities of the eCitaro, and decision-making in uncertain times.

title: BAIC Foton launches fast-charging ecosystem for electric trucks
summary: Megawatt charging is at the centre of BAIC Foton's plans for a fast-charging ecosystem for electric trucks. The Chinese commercial vehicle manufacturer is presenting a range of light- and heavy-duty vehicles alongside a fast-charging network that it intends to expand into markets beyond China, including Europe.

title: UK order books open for refreshed electric Volvos
summary: Volvo Car UK has just launched the refreshed 40 series range, now available for order in the UK. On-the-road prices start at £43,860 for the EX40 and £45,860 for the EC40.

title: Northumberland to sport 36 more public charge points
summary: A new suite of electric vehicle chargers is being added to Northumberland County Council's existing network. The Council has passed a motion to add an additional 36 EV charging points at 26 locations. The picturesque coastal region in the Northeast of England, borders Scotland and is famous for being home to Hadrian's wall and the Northumberland National Park.

title: Norwegian operator Torghatten Nord takes delivery of electric ferry Misterøy
summary: Norwegian shipping company Torghatten Nord from Tromsø has taken delivery of its new electric ferry named Misterøy. The nearly 77-meter-long Ro-Pax vessel was built at a Turkish shipyard and can transport up to 60 cars and 195 passengers. Two sister ships are set to follow.

title: BMW i3 completes North Cape to Tarifa journey with less than three hours of charging time
summary: BMW completed a nearly 5,900-kilometer journey from the North Cape to Tarifa with the new i3 50 xDrive. According to the manufacturer, the electric 3-series required a total of only 2 hours and 46 minutes for recharging.

title: Confusion over continued production of the VW ID.3 in Zwickau, Germany
summary: The ID.3 will also be built exclusively in Volkswagen's Zwickau plant in 2027, with the exception of the GTI variant, according to a statement made by Volkswagen’s Deputy Works Council Chairman Jürgen Mahnkopf yesterday at an automotive congress in Zwickau. Despite the worker's organisation's statment, the spokesperson for Volkswagen Sachsen has now denied the claim — and has made a point of emphasizing that ID.3 producton will move to the German carmaking giant's home of Wolfsburg next year.

title: ACEA Statistics show electric vans gain ground in EU
summary: The European van market is stagnating, but plug-in models are gaining significant ground. In the first nine months of 2026, their new registrations in the EU increased by 38.2 percent to nearly 152,000 vehicles.

title: DPD UK expands electric fleet with 381 new Fords from November
summary: DPD UK is further expanding its electric fleet. After 341 new Mercedes-Benz eSprinters already entered service with the delivery company in September 2026, DPD UK has now also ordered 381 Ford E-Transits. The electric vans are expected to be deployed starting mid-November.

title: Verne robotaxi service prepares for launch in Berlin
summary: Robotaxi provider Verne is preparing to launch in Germany, starting with the capital. The Croatian company told electrive that it is building its operational presence in the country. Two job postings for the Berlin location provide clues about the structures it intends to establish. Verne has not yet announced a specific launch date.

title: Mercedes-Benz high-power charging gains traction in the USA
summary: For its third anniversary in the USA, Mercedes-Benz High-Power Charging has taken stock. Within 36 months, the German automaker's infrastructure grew from a handful of test stations to a charging network of 100 locations and 934 charging points with a total of 245,000 customers.
